title: Android on the VM (redroid)
question: What was measured for Android on the VM (redroid)?
method: Transcribed from the cited historical record. Units and precision follow the source.

rows: Browser baseline on the VM (Playwright headless shell, the shared Metro web page, 15 s virtual-time budget, 3 runs): 169 s on first load while Metro compiled, then 5.6 s and 4.8 s wall, 628 and 636 MB peak RSS. User-mode QEMU TCG of a CPU loop on the same host: 0.41 s native, 4.0 s emulated, about 10 times slower. `/dev/kvm` is absent. `binder_linux` from `linux-modules-extra-6.17.0-1020-oracle` loads with `insmod` (approved by the owner) and Android's init starts, but redroid cannot boot in the `agent-dind` daemon: Android's `libprocessgroup` writes to `cgroup.procs` fail with ENOTSUP because every cgroup there is under a threaded cgroup root (`/sys/fs/cgroup` reads `domain threaded`, `--cgroup-parent` does not help). No redroid boot time or memory was measured, so the 5 times rule is not decided by numbers. Removing `binder_linux` fails with "Device or resource busy" (the module stays loaded until the VM reboots; nothing uses it).
